messages:
Maria (AE): Heads up — NovaBank RFP final round. They sent a 50-row security questionnaire and explicitly asked for our capability grid + POC runbook by EOD Fri. Can folks confirm who owns which sections and any hard blockers?
Kevin (Solutions): On it. Quick clarifying Qs: they listed 10k qps for embeddings and ~500 concurrent chat sessions during peak trading windows. Do we propose Dedicated + burst overlay or Hosted with Dedicated fallback?
Alex (Product): Recommend Dedicated with burst overlay for predictable throughput. I'll prepare two columns in the matrix: 'Reserved (Committed)' and 'Burst overlay'. Fields to include: burst scaling, KV cache, quantization options, model pinning, region failover.
Priya (Security): They asked specifically about HSM + customer-managed keys for Private. We support KMS in hosted; HSM is available for Private/on‑prem but requires customer appliance or partner HSM. I'll draft wording.
Sam (Finance): Pricing input: they want a 12mo committed contract + 15% discount and POC credits. How many committed token units does the 10k qps translate to? Need rough calc to price the tiers.
Alex (Product): Back-of-envelope: assume 80 tokens/response, 500 concurrent * 2 responses/sec => ~80M tokens/day peak. For monthly committed: that's ~2.4B tokens/mo peak — will sketch tier options and a smaller pilot band.
Maria (AE): Also, NovaBank flagged EU data residency and FedRAMP moderate as ask items. @Jenna — can Legal confirm FedRAMP posture and if we can provide standard wording?
Jenna (Legal): We are not FedRAMP-moderate as a hosted service. For Private/on‑prem deployments we can help customers meet FedRAMP controls via a customized engagement; that'll be an out-of-band attestation and likely adds time/cost. I'll draft the explanatory language.
Kevin (Solutions): Uploading a first draft runbook and the capability_grid draft: https://drive.redwood/reports/novabank-cap-grid-v1 — please review. Sample runbook includes test harness, load steps, auth setup.
deploy-bot: file uploaded: novabank_capability_grid_v1.xlsx
Priya (Security): For the questionnaire: 'key rotation' answer => hosted: automatic rotation via KMS (customer config); private: customer-controlled rotation. 'Audit logs retention' — propose 90/365/custom retention options. I'll add those rows.
Sam (Finance): I've started a pricing sheet. Offering: 12mo committed + 2-week POC credits that cap at pilot usage (we can offer a 30% smaller cap). Need to confirm cancel/refund language for pilot. Will attach calc.
Maria (AE): Next steps: Alex updates matrix + POC runbook by 8pm PST tonight; Priya + Jenna finalize security Qs and the FedRAMP paragraph; Sam sends initial commercial slide. If anything blocks, ping me immediately.
Alex (Product): Ack. Quick product question: for 'fallback model' column — should we explicitly state we support automatic fallback to a quantized compatible variant and adjust SLOs, or keep it vague?
Kevin (Solutions): Call out it is supported: 'automatic fallback to compatible model variants (quantized or smaller architectures) with graceful degradation; routing policy controls SLO adjustments and cost tradeoffs'. I'll add a short note and sample routing snippet.
Kevin (Solutions): Code snippet for matrix header (for copy/paste):
```
feature,supported,notes
burst_scaling,yes,Reserved pool + overlay burst (policy configurable)
kv_cache,yes,Prefix/KV caching for low-latency reuse
quantization,yes,Multiple quantization profiles available
model_pin,yes,Pin exact model versions per route
region_failover,yes,Automated failover with capacity fallback
```
Jenna (Legal): Also adding standard indemnity and regulated-data clause; legal will send a tracked-changes SOW.
Maria (AE): :thumbsup: Thanks team — I'll assemble the response package to NovaBank and ask for a 24-hour clarification window. If we get new security rows, drop them into the drive doc and @Priya.
